source.title: Understanding approximate Fisher information for fast convergence of natural gradient descent in wide neural networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including supplementary materials.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes and reports training convergence for natural-gradient methods with approximate Fisher matrices, using a different optimizer and loss setup from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports asymptotic convergence results and experiments for wide fully connected networks trained with natural gradient descent and MSE loss. It does not test the listed CIFAR classification, local-minimum, shortcut, initialization, learning-rate stability, or batch-normalization versions. Figure 1 and Figure S.1 show convergence curves without tabulated numeric values; the rows below record the paper's explicit textual results.
record.test_reason: The study establishes convergence properties of natural-gradient methods in wide fully connected networks. These results do not test any listed version: they do not measure the specified SGD/Adam classification outcomes, teacher-student minima, shortcut effects, initialization comparisons, above-threshold recovery, or batch-normalization effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: selected approximate Fisher methods match exact NGD's fast convergence under specific infinite-width conditions because their updates are isotropic in function space. The reported block tri-diagonal instability is also accurately described.
record.recipe_differences: Uses natural gradient descent with exact or approximate Fisher information and MSE loss, rather than the SGD/Adam classification recipes and other settings in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: For block tri-diagonal NGD, convergence depends on depth: L = 4 approaches the zero-damping dynamics, while L = 5 becomes unstable as damping approaches zero. K-FAC isotropy depends on input dimension and, when M0 < N, preprocessing. Unit-wise convergence relies on stated assumptions and a width-dependent damping schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Exact NGD and selected approximate-Fisher methods have matching rapid MSE convergence under stated wide-network assumptions and appropriately scaled learning rates. Block tri-diagonal NGD becomes unstable at L = 5 as damping approaches zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected Fisher approximations preserve exact natural-gradient convergence in wide fully connected networks under specific assumptions; convergence depends on approximation, damping, and learning-rate scaling.

record.problems: The principal convergence claims are asymptotic and rely on specific assumptions; the unit-wise proof uses the gradient independence assumption. Numerical convergence curves are plotted without tabulated values, and experiments use small two-class MNIST settings rather than the benchmark classification settings in the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying training-convergence results were omitted. Figure 3 compares isotropy condition numbers for Fisher approximations, not training-error outcomes, so it is not extracted as a row.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the listed claim versions; the study's own convergence and divergence findings remain valid observations. No qualifying result for V1–V6 is missing.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error; convolutional networks; SGD or Adam; corrupted or random labels; smaller models and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, depth-related training error, and normalization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, and the specified plain-network depth comparisons.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature changes, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effect on speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: deep fully-connected neural networks (exact pseudo-inverse NGD)
rows.size_stated: infinite-width limit; sufficiently large hidden-layer widths
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical analysis of exact pseudo-inverse natural gradient descent with MSE loss on training samples.
rows.value: The training dynamics converge to f∞(x) = y, with zero training error.
rows.uncertainty: with high probability in the sufficiently large width analysis
rows.note: The paper states this as a theoretical result for exact NGD; it is not a classification-error result.
rows.check: Exact-NGD convergence is established in Section 3.3 and Supplement A.3, but it does not measure any version's effect. Section 3.1's zero-error GD result summarizes prior work and should not be attributed to this study.

rows.subject: deep fully-connected neural networks (block-diagonal NGD)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical and experimental training with a block-diagonal layer-wise approximate Fisher matrix.

conditions.value: two-class MNIST (‘0’ and ‘7’), N = 100 in Figure 1

rows.value: The block-diagonal approximation achieves the same convergence rate as exact NGD with learning rate scaled by 1/L; the text says the numerical dynamics coincide well with the theoretical dynamics.
rows.note: The loss curves in Figure 1(a) are not numerically tabulated.
rows.check: This compares optimizer convergence rates, outside the listed versions. The experimental baseline should include GD at its stated optimal learning rate; BD-NGD also converges faster at the tested suboptimal rate.

rows.subject: deep fully-connected neural networks (block tri-diagonal NGD), L = 4
rows.operation_detail: Training with a block tri-diagonal approximate Fisher matrix and damping sweep.
rows.value: Training dynamics got closer to those for ρ = 0 as the damping term decreased to zero.
rows.note: The plotted loss values are not numerically tabulated.
rows.check: Agreement with zero-damping NGD dynamics measures sensitivity to a Fisher approximation, not any version's depth, initialization, or stability effect.

rows.subject: deep fully-connected neural networks (block tri-diagonal NGD), L = 5
rows.operation_detail: Training with a block tri-diagonal approximate Fisher matrix and damping sweep.
rows.value: The training dynamics exploded as the damping term became close to zero.
rows.note: The paper attributes this behavior to singularity of the block tri-diagonal Fisher matrix when L = 5.
rows.check: The reported divergence as damping decreases is accurate, but it is not a reversal of any listed version. Neither recovery above an initial stability threshold nor the plain-versus-residual depth comparison is tested.

rows.subject: deep fully-connected neural networks (K-FAC NGD)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical analysis of K-FAC with MSE loss; numerical experiments evaluate predictions of the trained model.

conditions.value: M0 ≥ N and input samples linearly independent for the stated isotropic result
C = 1 for the main K-FAC result

rows.value: The isotropic condition holds, Θ̄ = NLI, and K-FAC achieves fast convergence under the stated assumptions.
rows.note: For M0 < N, the paper states that naive settings are not isotropic; a Forster transformation restores the isotropic condition.
rows.check: K-FAC isotropy and convergence are properties of the study's optimizer under input-rank assumptions; they do not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: deep fully-connected neural networks (unit-wise NGD)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical and experimental training with a unit-wise approximate Fisher matrix.

conditions.value: Tanh; ReLU; shifted ReLU with s = 1 in Figure S.1
gradient independence assumption in the theoretical result

rows.value: Theorem 5.1 gives asymptotic convergence to the target under η = c/α, 0 < c < 2; the text says the experimental dynamics show excellent agreement with the theory.
rows.locator: Section 5; Supplementary Materials C.2.2 and Figure S.1
rows.note: The plotted loss values are not numerically tabulated. The result depends on the stated assumption and damping schedule.
rows.check: Unit-wise NGD convergence does not test a listed version. Activation-dependent learning-rate scaling is not a comparison of initialization schemes. The numbers_found value '1/1' has no identified result interpretation and should be removed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
